title: Queue frostline benchmark notes
summary: Short notes from an informal experiment exploring a phenomenon where small increases in ingress cause a sudden jump in tail latency that looks like a 'frostline' forming in the queueing layer. Goal: reproduce, characterize thresholds, and get candidate mitigations for staging rollout.
hypothesis: A narrow region of offered load produces queue-length correlations across worker shards that amplify KV-cache misses and force synchronous slow-path tokenization, producing a steep p95/p99 cliff (the "frostline"). Secondary hypothesis: uneven shard priming (cold KV) + CPU scheduler tail effects magnify this.
setup: Cluster: 4x p4d (48 vCPU, 8x A100) dev pool. Runtime: serving-runtime v2.9.3 (opt kernels on). Model: bloom-7B (quantized int8), context 2048. Ingress generator: rps-sim v0.7 generating synthetic text-gen requests, 1–8 tokens avg output. Context: prefix cache disabled for first run, enabled in second. Batch settings: max_batch_tokens=4096, max_latency_ms=50. Background noise: 10% low-priority background requests to simulate multi-tenant jitter.
run_plan: baseline: steady poisson arrival at 120 qps for 10m (cache primed)
ramp: linear ramp 10->180 qps over 8m, hold 3m at peak, then step down
microbursts: add 5x spikes of 500 qps for 2s spaced 30s apart
shard-imbalance: artificially delay one worker's cache fill (30s) to simulate cold shard
config-variants: prefix_cache on/off, max_latency_ms 25/50/100, batch window 5/10ms
observations:
1) At ~150 qps during ramp the p95/p99 suddenly diverged; p95 went from 30ms->110ms while p99 exploded. This aligns with a sharp rise in queue_depth_mean and KV cache hit drop.
2) Microbursts push queue depth into a regime where backlog across shards aligns (we saw cross-shard queue correlation).
3) When one shard had delayed cache priming the whole service showed earlier frostline onset (lower global qps when cliff hit).
4) Tighter max_latency_ms decreased batching which reduced token amortization and moved the cliff earlier (bad).
5) Enabling prefix cache moved the cliff right (higher tolerated qps) but not elimination; cache hotter shards still dominated overall behavior.
6) Some traces show long tail from a 40ms syscall spike on workers (cpu scheduler jitter) coincident with KV miss storms.
quick_conclusions: The 'frostline' is a systemic effect: queue correlation + cache miss storms + batching policy interact nonlinearly.
Mitigation should be multi-pronged: prioritize fast cache priming across shards, introduce staggered small-batch preemption to protect latency SLOs, and guard microbursts with ingress shaping.
Tightening max_latency for lower latency SLOs can backfire by reducing amortization; prefer smarter early-exit/priority lanes rather than single global latency knob.
next_steps: Run micro-experiments with explicit shard-affinity to verify if isolating tenants to shards delays or removes frostline.
Prototype a tiny preemption hook: allow a small fraction of long-wait tokens to be requeued and served by a fast-path lane.
Instrument syscall latency and CPU-scheduler jitter on workers during runs (use perf + eBPF tracepoints).
Draft a short proposal for product: 'Frostline guardrails' - ingress shaping + shard priming + preemptive fast lane (2 pager).
raw_command_log:
# example load command
./rps-sim --target http://staging-infer:8080/gen --qps 150 --duration 600 --payload templates/simple.json
# ramp script
./rps-sim --ramp 10:180 --ramp-duration 480 --hold 180 --payload templates/simple.json
# collect traces
curl http://metrics:9090/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])) > p99.txt
# priming script to warm shards (run on all workers)
python tools/kv_prime.py --model bloom-7B --batch 8 --duration 60
notes_to_self: Keep this doc lightweight — save full traces in S3 under s3://redwood-perf/queue-frostline/lucia/ (tag runs with trace-id). Share quick slide with SRE and product next week. If we can show even a 15% delay in frostline with shard priming + ingress shaping that's a strong case for incremental rollout.
